newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL PENALTY GIVES ZIMBABWE THE SPOILS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL PENALTY GIVES ZIMBABWE THE SPOILS.

text.p: Zimbabwe put themselves back in contention for a place in the African Nations Cup finals with a controversial 1-0 win over Angola in Harare on Sunday.
Wilfred Mugeyi, who had his initial penalty attempt saved by Angolan goalkeeper Marito, was given a second chance to score after Angolan defender Paulao was penalised for encroaching in the area.

There was no disputing the awarding of the initial penalty, which came after Helder Vicente had handled a cross by Adam Ndlovu, but the Angolans protested heatedly when a retake of the spotkick was ordered.
Madagascan referee Milton Josy was surrounded by furious players and pushed and shoved but stood firm on his decision.

Mugeyi, playing in the starting line-up for the first time, made no mistake with the second attempt to earn a victory which put Zimbabwe level on points with Ghana at the top of the group one standings.
Mugeyi's twin brother William was also drafted into the team.
Zimbabwe, who played the game at a cracking pace despite the searing heat, had only two other clear chances, both shots by Swiss-based striker Agent Sawu which went narrowly wide.
Angola, who played with a lone striker, might well have snatched a late equaliser had substitute Quinzinho got onto the end of a Carlos Pedro cross.
Zimbabwe's coach Ian Porterfield said he was satisfied with the performance, despite the absence of the team's two English-based players Bruce Grobbelaar and Peter Ndlovu.
Goalkeeper Grobbelaar did not travel because his match-fixing trial in England is nearing completion while Ndlovu is refusing to play because of a dispute over payment.
"The team is improving and while we have played better in other games, we deserved to win," said Porterfield.

The Angolans complained bitterly after the match but Portuguese-based midfielder Chipenda admitted the pace of the home's game had proved a handful. "They were better than us but we are not out of the competition yet."
Ghana and Zimbabwe top the group with four points each while Angola have lost both their opening matches. But the Angolans still have two home encounters to play in the three-team group.

Zimbabwe: 16-Gift Muzadzi; 2-Lloyd Chitembwe, 3-Edelbert Dinha, 5-Dumisani Mpofu, 15-Norman Mapeza, 6-Francis Shonhayi; 14-William Mugeyi, 11-Kennedy Chihuri (4-Benjamin Nkonjera 70th min), 13-Adam Ndlovu (8-Vitalis Takawira 83rd); 10-Wilfred Mugeyi, 12-Agent Sawu.
